title: Oligohydramnios and Potter: a sequence
vignette: A newborn boy is being evaluated in the delivery room due to respiratory distress. He was born at 37 weeks gestation to a 28-year-old primigravida via cesarean delivery due to breech presentation. The mother had limited prenatal care but was noted to have oligohydramnios during pregnancy. Examination of the infant is significant for a flattened nose and ears, recessed chin, and bilateral clubfoot deformity. Breath sounds are decreased bilaterally. This pattern of findings is best classified as which of the following?

clues.note: Low amniotic fluid (oligohydramnios) is the PRIMARY inciting event. It causes fetal compression, and the downstream anomalies all follow from that single mechanical cause - the definition of a sequence.

clues.text: flattened nose and ears, recessed chin
clues.note: Flattened facies (flat nose, low-set ears, recessed chin) results from extrinsic compression by the low fluid - part of the Potter sequence cascade.
Limb deformities (clubfoot, contractures) arise from restricted fetal movement in a compressed uterus - another downstream effect of oligohydramnios.
Pulmonary hypoplasia (from restricted thoracic expansion) causes respiratory distress and decreased breath sounds - the most severe, often fatal, component of Potter sequence.

whatMatters: Oligohydramnios -> fetal compression -> flattened facies + limb deformities (clubfoot) + pulmonary hypoplasia = Potter SEQUENCE. A sequence is a cascade of anatomically related anomalies all arising from ONE primary anomaly/inciting event (here, low amniotic fluid). Answer E.
strategy: Match the pattern to the definition. Because ONE primary event (oligohydramnios) causes a predictable chain of related anomalies (cause-and-effect), it's a SEQUENCE. Contrast: association = anomalies co-occurring more than by chance with NO known cause (VACTERL); syndrome = anomalies from one underlying (usually genetic) cause developing INDEPENDENTLY; dysplasia = abnormal tissue organization; mosaicism = two genetically distinct cell lines.

eliminations.label: Association - co-occurrence, no known cause, your pick
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an association is >=2 anomalies that occur together more often than by chance but WITHOUT a known unifying cause (e.g., VACTERL). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: here there IS a known primary cause (oligohydramnios) driving a cascade - that's a sequence, not an association. ✅ Correct if: VACTERL or another non-random co-occurrence without an identified cause.

eliminations.label: Dysplasia - abnormal tissue organization
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: dysplasia is abnormal cellular/tissue organization or growth (e.g., skeletal dysplasia). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: Potter findings are mechanical deformations from compression, not a tissue-organization defect. ✅ Correct if: a primary abnormal-tissue-growth disorder.

eliminations.label: Mosaicism - two cell lines
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: mosaicism is the presence of two or more genetically distinct cell populations in one individual. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this is a mechanical cascade, not a genetic-mosaic phenomenon. ✅ Correct if: mosaic Turner/Down syndrome.

eliminations.label: Polymorphism - normal genetic variation
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a polymorphism is a common normal genetic variant in a population (e.g., eye color). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it doesn't describe a pattern of birth defects. ✅ Correct if: describing benign genetic variation.

reasoning: Oligohydramnios is a single primary inciting event
It mechanically compresses the fetus, producing a predictable, related cascade of anomalies
Flattened facies + clubfoot + pulmonary hypoplasia all follow from that one cause (cause-and-effect)
-> this is a sequence (Potter sequence); answer E
mechanism: A sequence is a predictable pattern of multiple anatomically related anomalies that develop as a consequence of a single primary anomaly or mechanical event (a cause-and-effect cascade). In Potter sequence, oligohydramnios - often from a genitourinary anomaly (e.g., bilateral renal agenesis) impairing fetal urine production, or from preterm rupture of membranes - reduces amniotic fluid so the fetus is compressed. This mechanical constraint produces the characteristic downstream findings: pulmonary hypoplasia (restricted thoracic expansion -> respiratory distress, often fatal), flattened facies (flat nasal bridge, low-set ears, recessed chin), and limb deformities such as clubfoot and contractures. Because all findings stem from one inciting event, this is a sequence - distinct from an association (co-occurring anomalies without a known cause, e.g., VACTERL), a syndrome (anomalies from a single underlying, often genetic, cause developing independently), dysplasia (abnormal tissue organization), or mosaicism (two genetically distinct cell lines).
